stories.title: Neo4j Context Engine Launches to Create AI Knowledge Layer and Enhance Agent Performance
stories.body: On October 20, 2026, Neo4j launched the Context Engine in private preview — a reusable, shared knowledge-layer substrate that lets AI agents consistently reason over enterprise data across existing platforms, catalogs, and storage systems. The product ships with a six-layer Business Ontology for mapping what a company means by entities like 'customer' or 'supplier,' a Context Studio governance console, and a graph-native memory layer that logs agent reasoning and turns repeated decision patterns into reusable knowledge. Neo4j's CPO stated that modeling relationships and showing exactly why they exist is 'absolutely essential to solving the problem of context for AI,' and that all other approaches 'break as AI agents grow in complexity.'
stories.why: This is the clearest recent proof that the context-layer category has hardened from thesis to product: a named vendor with an enterprise graph sales motion has shipped a buyable object at exactly the layer Graas occupies. A seller can use this to explain to prospects why agents fail without a governed knowledge layer — and position Graas as the retail-domain equivalent before Neo4j's generalist motion lands in their account.

stories.tag: US - analyst research / why pilots stall
stories.title: McKinsey State of AI 2026: 89% Use AI, Only 6% See Real Enterprise Returns — Scaling Rises but EBIT Impact Flat
stories.body: McKinsey's 2026 State of AI report (1,719 respondents, 97 countries, published August 2026) finds that 89% of organizations use AI in at least one business function, and 44% say it is scaling across the enterprise — up from 38% — yet the share reporting any EBIT impact is stuck at 37% and only about 6% qualify as 'high performers' attributing significant company-wide profit to AI. Eighty percent of respondents say AI improved their personal productivity, but McKinsey identifies a classic implementation gap: benefits exist at the task level but are not flowing through to business outcomes because workflows have not been redesigned and AI investments sit on top of old operating models. Separately, McKinsey's State of Organizations 2026 found 86% of leaders say their organizations are not very prepared to adopt AI in day-to-day operations, and just one in six have a clear C-level owner for AI adoption.
stories.why: This is the sharpest quantified case for why retail AI pilots stall: the data problem is not model capability but operating-model readiness and data foundation. Sellers can open a call by citing these numbers to validate the prospect's frustration, then pivot to how a context/data layer is what converts pilot productivity into measurable P&L — which is exactly what Graas provides.

stories.tag: US - analyst research / agentic retail merchandising
stories.title: BCG: 'Always-On Merchandising' — Agentic AI Can Shrink Category Decisions from Weeks to Hours, But Only if Retailers Redesign Data and Operating Models First
stories.body: In an April 2026 report, BCG argues that specialized, connected AI agents can perform core merchandising tasks — pricing, promotions, assortment, and inventory — turning a slow, siloed process into an always-on system, with agentic systems potentially shrinking decisions from weeks to hours by continuously sensing and responding to market signals. BCG's AI Radar survey of 2,400 global executives found nearly all CEOs believe AI agents will produce measurable returns in 2026, and four in five are more optimistic about AI ROI than a year ago. However, BCG explicitly warns that agents only deliver this value if retailers redesign their strategy, data, and operating model alongside the technology — not just layer agents onto legacy systems.
stories.why: BCG is naming the same pre-condition Graas sells: agents require a redesigned data and operating model underneath them, not just a chatbot on top of a legacy stack. A seller can cite this report to give a CIO or CMO analyst cover for investing in the data foundation before — or alongside — the agent layer, reducing the 'let's start with just the agent' objection.

stories.tag: US - named CPG enterprise deployment with outcomes
stories.title: Tredence Agentic AI Recovers $6.5M from $40M in Addressable CPG Trade Deductions, Delivering 60% ORM Productivity Gain
stories.body: Tredence deployed a multi-agent deduction-management system for a leading global CPG brand whose Order and Revenue Management team processed between 87,000 and 157,000 payment deductions annually, with individual claims ranging from $150 to over $50,000. The system integrated across 30-plus APIs spanning SAP, EDI, retailer portals, and email; a reasoning engine mapped customer scenarios to internal reason codes, and an analytical agent assessed investigation feasibility and write-offs — recovering $6.5M from roughly $40M in addressable deduction spend and delivering a 60% productivity gain across ORM operations. Tredence describes the approach as a multi-agent system where each agent specializes in a domain while sharing a common data model, rather than one generalist agent attempting every task.
stories.why: This is a named, outcome-quantified enterprise CPG deployment of a multi-agent system grounded in a shared data model — the architecture argument Graas makes in every sales call. Sellers can use the $6.5M recovery and 60% productivity figures as a retail/CPG-specific proof point that agents grounded in unified data produce real P&L outcomes, not just demo metrics.

stories.tag: US - agent vendor / Sierra & Decagon competitive landscape
stories.title: Sierra Reaches $200M ARR and $15.8B Valuation After $950M Round; Decagon Grows to $100M ARR at $4.5B — Intercom Fin Acquired by Salesforce for ~$3.6B
stories.body: In May 2026, Sierra raised $950M at a $15.8B valuation led by Tiger Global and GV, reaching approximately $200M ARR and counting over 40% of the Fortune 50 as customers; it charges roughly $1.50 per resolution and requires multi-year enterprise contracts with a ~$150K annual floor. Rival Decagon tripled its valuation to $4.5B in a $250M January 2026 round led by Coatue and Index Ventures, grew from $44M ARR at end-2025 to $100M ARR by July 2026, and added more than 100 corporate clients in the prior year including Avis Budget Group and Deutsche Telekom. The most structurally significant event in the category was Salesforce's agreement to acquire Intercom's Fin business for roughly $3.6B in June 2026, consolidating the per-outcome pricing model inside the world's largest CRM platform.
stories.why: Three competitive dynamics are now live in every enterprise CX evaluation: Sierra's Palantir-style embedded-engineer model at $150K+ floors, Decagon's lighter-procurement challenger, and Fin now embedded in Salesforce at $0.99/outcome. Sellers need to know where Graas sits relative to these vendors — and can position the absence of a retail-domain knowledge layer in all three as the gap Graas fills before any of them can work reliably in complex retail and CPG environments.
